questions.question: OP-01/O51 (Closed order): D80 puts argument checks first 'in every state but Closed', so a caller error on a Closed stream is undecided. On a closed CPython BufferedReader, read('x') raises TypeError and read(2) ValueError. On a Closed stream, which comes first?

options.label: Args first, as io (Recommended)
options.description: A caller error is raised first in every state, Closed included; a valid call on a Closed stream raises ValueError (D15). Matches io, whose contract D70 adopts, and D80's adopted option 'one rule for every state'.

options.label: Closed first
options.description: Every call on a Closed stream raises ValueError whatever its arguments, as D80's Decision reads. Differs from io for a wrong-typed argument.

questions.question: OP-01/O51 (Failed calls): D52 says 'every read on a Failed stream raises' and D80 'a valid call on a Failed stream raises the failure again', which reads as covering close(), tell(), readable() and seekable() too. Which calls raise the failure again on a Failed stream?

options.label: Data reads only (Recommended)
options.description: read, read1, readinto, readline, line iteration and chunks raise it again (D52). close releases and leaves it Closed (D16, D18). tell returns the bytes delivered so far, readable is true, seekable false, and seek/truncate/write raise io.UnsupportedOperation. Each of these answers stays true after a failure and makes no request.

options.label: All but close
options.description: Every call but close raises it again, tell/readable/seekable included. A caller that only probes the stream learns of the failure, but a wrapper that probes readable() fails when built rather than at its first read.

questions.question: OP-01/O59 (cancelled close): D49 and D50 leave a stream Closed after a cancelled close(), but D50's dialog offered only 'a read is cancelled'. What state is a stream in after its close() is cancelled?

options.label: Closed (Recommended)
options.description: The cancellation propagates (D49) and the stream is Closed, its resources released or abandoned; a second close is a no-op. Source: io.IOBase.close marks the file closed even when its flush raises.

options.label: State before close
options.description: The stream stays Open, Exhausted or Failed and the caller must close it again. A cancelled 'async with' exit then holds the connection until the stream is collected (D17).

questions.question: OP-01/O59 (re-raised type): for a failure raised as is (a MemoryError, an OSError with errno EMFILE), D52 raises again 'of the original's type', where its dialog option said 'of the same category'. What does a Failed stream raise again for such a failure?

options.label: Type and args (Recommended)
options.description: A new exception of the original's type, built from its args, so an OSError keeps its errno; the original is its __cause__. Such a failure's only category is its type, so the option and the Decision agree. Source: D52, OSError's constructor (errno from args).

options.label: Type only
options.description: A new exception of the original's type, with no args; errno is reachable only through __cause__.

options.label: Wrapped
options.description: The store's base category with the original as its cause. 'except MemoryError' then no longer catches the failure when it is raised again.

options.description: Every call on a Closed stream raises ValueError whatever its arguments, as D80's Decision reads. Differs from io for a wrong-typed argument.
options.label: Closed first

OP-01/O58 (read1 in D18): D18's read column lists read, readinto, readline and chunks but not read1, which D70 adds and which draws from the same position. How does D18's state table cover read1?

options.label: One data-read column (Recommended)
options.description: The column reads: every method that draws from the position, which is read, read1, readinto, readline, line iteration and chunks. Its cells stay as they are.

options.label: Own column
options.description: read1 gets a column of its own whose cells repeat read's. Same behaviour, a wider table.

questions.question: OP-01/O58 (async methods): D69 makes read, readinto, readline, read1 and close coroutines and tell, readable and seekable plain methods. No dialog asked that plain-methods sentence; its option read 'Same methods, awaited'. seek, truncate and write are in neither list. In the async stream, which methods are coroutines?

options.label: All awaited (Recommended)
options.description: Every method is a coroutine, including tell, readable, seekable, seek, truncate and write (the last three raise io.UnsupportedOperation when awaited). One rule, as D69's option read. Source: aiofiles runs every file method as a coroutine, tell, readable and seekable included (not run).

options.label: No-request ones plain
options.description: tell, readable, seekable, seek, truncate and write are plain methods (the last three raise when called); the others are coroutines, as D69's Decision reads. Cheaper to call, but not the option the dialog offered.

options.label: anyio's split
options.description: tell, seek, truncate and write are awaited; readable and seekable are plain, as anyio's AsyncFile has them (not run).

questions.question: OP-01/O52 (phase lists): D79 lets a whole read surface every D34 row except changed and a closed stream's ValueError, but D35's sentence 'a whole read surfaces everything' still stands. D46's open-call list keeps the closed-stream ValueError. D46's check says the open's and a read's lists overlap only in what a backend request can meet, though both also hold the caller errors and a cancellation. How are D35 and D46 brought in line?

options.label: Amend both (Recommended)
options.description: D35's whole-read sentence reads as D79 does. D46's open list also leaves out a closed stream's ValueError. D46's check reads: the two lists overlap in what any backend request can meet, the caller errors raised before contact, and a cancellation.

options.label: D79 governs, texts stay
options.description: D35 and D46 are left as they are, and D79 is read as superseding them. A spec author then meets two texts that disagree.

questions.question: OP-01/O59 (E16 exposure): D62 exposes E16 (an O3 metadata-only change) 'at s3 only, through a resume'. But D22's dialog has a stream need a new request when its connection is recycled or it resumes, and D47, D61 and D86 name any new backend request. Through which requests does E16 reach a stream?

options.label: Any new request (Recommended)
options.description: E16 reaches a stream through any new backend request the stream makes, a resume or otherwise, as D86 says for E18. How many requests a stream makes stays not promised (NP2).

options.label: Resume only
options.description: E16 reaches a stream only through a resume. That promises the stream makes no other new request, which goes against NP2.
